The '''Yangkaal language,''' also known as Yanggaralda,{{sfn|Tindale|1974|p=170}} Janggal, Gananggalinda, Nemarang, among other names, is an extinct [[Australian Aboriginal languages|Australian Aboriginal language]].<ref name="AIATSIS" /> [[Geoffrey O'Grady]] grouped it as a variety of [[Yukulta language|Yukulta]] within the [[Tangkic languages|Tangkic language family]].{{efn|'Tangkic Group Jakula-Njangga (Yanggal, Nyangga).'{{sfn|O'Grady|Voegelin|Voegelin|1966|p=54}}}} The implication was that "Yanggal" was simply an alternative name for "Njangga", which is an alternative [[ethnonym]] for the [[Yanyuwa people|Yanyula (Yanyuwa)]], from which the word Yanggal may have derived.{{sfn|Dixon|Blake|1983|p=193}}

== Vocabulary ==
* ''bidinaŋga'' (man)
* ''magudaŋga'' (woman)
* ''ganda'' (father)
* ''ŋama'' (mother).{{sfn|Capell|1942|p=50}}
